title: Zheng Yuanjie Returns After a Two-Year Hiatus: Uses AI to Hand-Craft Animations and Releases Them for Free, Also Urges Peers to Switch to Paid AI and Give It a Try

On November 17, Zheng Yuanjie, the “King of Fairy Tales,” who had not updated his self-media for two full years, suddenly returned. What he brought was not a new serialized work, but something even he found unbelievable—although he knew nothing about animation production, he used AI to turn his fairy tales into animated shorts. He has authorized the Douyin account “Zheng Yuanjie’s Fairy Tale World” (Douyin ID: 83425404836) to release these shorts so readers can watch them for free. Several animated clips are currently posted on the account, mainly adapted from his Chinese zodiac fairy tales and children’s popular science content.

Free Is an Unstoppable Trend Through this experiment, Zheng Yuanjie offered a judgment: under the wave of AI technology, free enjoyment of cultural and intellectual works has become an unstoppable historical trend. His logic is simple—a writer who knows nothing about animation can use AI to create cartoons that replace professional animators, and people who know nothing about literature can also use AI to write decent works. The saying “Read ten thousand books, and your pen will be guided as if by the gods” is the perfect description of AI. Universal participation in creation is irreversible, because cultural and intellectual works have always been the common wealth of all humanity.

A Warning, a Congratulation There is also a sharp edge in his words: he reminds colleagues who do not believe AI can make writers unemployed—the AI you use to test writing is surely free AI. Switch to the most expensive paid AI and try again, and I guarantee you will be so anxious you cannot sleep at night. At the end of the video, he left his blessings to the post-00s generation: you have truly caught up with a great era of equal access to knowledge, where cultural and intellectual works can be enjoyed for free and everyone can participate in creation without barriers. From Pipilu and Shuke to Beita, this writer who has influenced generations of readers now chooses to stand on the side of the wave.
